div.l: We dronke / and to reste wente echon
Withoute eny / lenger tariynge
A morwe whan the day / bigan to sprynge
Vp roos oure host and was oure alther cok
And andand gadered vs / to gider in a flok
And forth we riden / a litel more than pas
Vn to the waterynge / of seint thomas
And than oure host / gan his hors areste
And seide lordinges / herkeneth ȝif ȝow leste
Ȝe woot ȝoure forward / and I it recorde
Ȝif euensong and morwe song accorde
Lat se now / who shal telle the firste tale
As eủere mote I drynke / wyn or ale
Who so be rebel / to my iugement
Shal paye for al / that by the way is spent
Now draweth cut / or that we ferther twynne
Which that hath the shortest shal first begynne
¶ Sire knyght qd he / my maister and my lord
Now draweth cut for that is myn accord
Cometh ner qd he / my lady prioresse
And ȝe sir clerk / lat be ȝoure shamefastnesse
Ne studieth nought / ley hand to eủery man
Anon to drawe / eủery wight bigan
And shortly for to tellen / as it was
Were it by auenture / or sort or cas .
The sothe is this / the cut fel to the knyght
Of which ful blithe / and glad was eủery wyght
And tellen he muste his tale / as was resoıı̄un
¶ By forward / and by composicioıı̄un
As ȝe han herd / what nedeth wordes mo
And whan this good man / saugh that it was so
As he that wys was / and obedient
To kepen his forward / by his fre assent
He seide sitthen / I shal begynne the game
What welcome be the cut / in goddes name
Now lat vs ryde / and herkeneth what II seye
And with that word / we riden forth oure weye
And he bigan / right with a mery chere
His tale anon / and seide as ȝe may here
